analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side text of docs/reference/configuration.md (lines 348-728). The only changed range is a documentation-only edit at line 180, the scheduled serving windows row. It adds that, with consent, cached Autopilot builds verified at start or by the previous window's provider stay while their bytes hash unchanged. That line sits outside the supplied units, and the patch excerpt is truncated at the end of the row. I could therefore not see the full head wording or the source that the row cites. I examined the supplied base text for env-var and config contracts relevant to the threat model: prefix cache and SSD cache (T-041), auth token path (A-008), environment scrubbing (T-014), and the memory and media budgets. The text is unchanged and describes pre-existing controls, so I report no regression. The one open question is the edited row's semantics. If it describes code that skips re-attestation or re-verification of an Autopilot build between windows (TB-011, T-054, A-017), the actual code needs review. That would cover stale code-evidence reuse and whether 'bytes hash unchanged' is checked on every window against the qualified identity. This PR's diff contains no code, so I record the question as unverified rather than as a finding. A later pass should check ScheduledWindowSelection.swift and StartCommand+Modes.swift if they are part of the PR. Docs alone introduce no new attack surface.
